comparison: Both evaluate the same expression pattern claims (C3, C4, C31-C46, C78, C109, C110). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with strong converging evidence from Northern blots and in situ hybridization. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 raising major concerns about layer specificity claims and requesting normalized quantification across brain regions, finding the current quantification insufficient.

Both address migration and cell fate claims. OpenEval (C5, C48-C52, C112) finds migration defects SUPPORTED with quantitative binning analysis and layer-specific markers. Peer review (C5, C6, C49-C52, C54, C55, C112) rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 stating that 'functional analysis of miR-128 is only based on gain of function/overexpression experiments' and requesting loss-of-function evidence. Peer review also includes morphological claims (C6, C54, C55) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Perfect agreement on claims (C7, C53). OpenEval finds the sponge inhibitor loss-of-function data SUPPORTED, though notes mechanism validation could be improved. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging the bidirectional phenotype (gain-of-function causes undermigration, loss-of-function causes overmigration), though they request more comprehensive loss-of-function analysis.

OpenEval evaluates morphological claims (C6, C54, C55) as SUPPORTED based on 3D reconstruction and statistical analysis. Peer review groups these with migration claims and rates UNCERTAIN, requesting loss-of-function evidence to demonstrate that miR-128 is required for dendritic branching phenotypes.

Both address Phf6 as miR-128 target with overlapping claims (C11, C56-C60). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multiple converging lines of evidence (computational prediction, reporter assays, Western blots). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 stating 'The study does not provide compelling evidence that Phf6 is a target of miR-128 in the developing cortex' and noting that whether miR-128 normally regulates Phf6 in vivo is not addressed.

OpenEval includes temporal correlation data (C61-C63) in their SUPPORTED evaluation of Phf6 as a target. Peer review evaluates these claims separately as UNCERTAIN, stating that temporal correlation alone is insufficient and requesting direct demonstration of miR-128 regulation of Phf6 in developing cortex, including Phf6 protein expression patterns.

Both evaluate rescue experiments (C12, C64, C92). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, stating the rescue provides strong evidence for functional relationship and establishes causality. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 stating that 'the functional study of a putative miR-128-Phf6 pathway in cortical development does not stand on solid ground' because authors haven't demonstrated that miR-128 normally regulates Phf6 in vivo.

Both address dendritic phenotype claims (C8, C73-C76). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with rigorous 3D reconstruction, Sholl analysis, and PHF6 rescue demonstrating mechanistic specificity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 requesting loss-of-function evidence to demonstrate that miR-128 is required for normal dendritic development.

Both evaluate electrophysiological characterization with high overlap (C9, C65-C72, C96, C99-C103). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive measurements and appropriate rescue experiments. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, applying Reviewer 2's concern that functional analysis is only based on gain-of-function experiments and requesting loss-of-function validation.

Both address overarching conclusions (C15-C17, C80, C81, C82, C113). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by combined evidence from expression patterns, gain/loss-of-function, target validation, and rescue studies. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, challenged by Reviewer 1's statement that the pathway model doesn't stand on solid ground and Reviewer 2's request for loss-of-function data.

Both address interpretive/speculative claims. OpenEval (C77, C79, C93, C94) rates UNCERTAIN, noting that post-transcriptional regulation mechanism (DICER processing delay) is not directly tested and the regulatory switch concept is speculative. Peer review (C77, C79-C81, C93-C95, C104, C106, C107, C113) also rates UNCERTAIN, stating these interpretive claims are undermined by major concerns about the pathway model and go beyond what current data support.

Both evaluate background/literature claims. OpenEval (C1, C2, C18-C30) finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge providing necessary context. Peer review (C1, C2, C10, C18-C30, C83-C90, C97, C105) also rates SUPPORTED, acknowledging these provide relevant context and noting that reviewers recognize the identification of new miR-128 functions provides new insights.

OpenEval evaluates PHF6 background literature (C10, C83-C90, C97) as SUPPORTED, providing context for understanding PHF6 significance. Peer review groups these with other background claims and rates SUPPORTED, not challenging the established literature about PHF6.

Both address differential activity of miR-128 isoforms (C33, C34, C47, C108, C111). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as important technical finding for experimental design. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, treating this as a technical observation, though Reviewer 2 questions why exogenous pre-miR-128-2 is processed while endogenous is not.

OpenEval includes C47 (electroporated cells produce mature miR-128) in differential isoform activity evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer review evaluates C47 separately as SUPPORTED technical validation, though notes Reviewer 2's question about processing differences between exogenous and endogenous pre-miR-128-2.

Both address interpretive claims about complexity and limitations. OpenEval (C98-C100, C104) finds SUPPORTED, noting authors appropriately acknowledge complexity and that PHF6 is not sole mediator. Peer review (C79, C91, C98, C100, C103) rates UNCERTAIN, stating these speculative mechanistic claims are subject to concerns about the overall pathway model, with Reviewer 2 directly challenging processing mechanism speculation.

OpenEval evaluates comparison to prior work and synaptic changes (C105-C107) as SUPPORTED, though notes speculation about region/time-dependence. Peer review includes some of these claims (C106, C107) in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of interpretive claims that go beyond what data support according to reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates comparison to Zhang et al. 2013 (C91) as SUPPORTED, noting similarity in phenotypes supports regulatory relationship. Peer review includes C91 in UNCERTAIN evaluation of speculative mechanistic claims subject to concerns about the overall pathway model.
